page: Amazon Web Services c8gb.large is an entry-level compute-optimized virtual server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It utilizes two dedicated physical cores built on the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture with Neoverse-V2 cores operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. The processor configuration assigns one thread per core without hyperthreading, supported by 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache. Cryptographic processing is accelerated via hardware-level AES instructions.

Memory allocation stands at 4.0 GB total, delivering 2.0 GB per dedicated vCPU, aligning with standard compute-optimized resource ratios. The instance contains no integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, depending entirely on network-attached storage volumes for disk operations. Network performance is provisioned at a baseline capacity of 4 Gbps, while public IPv4 addresses are not included complimentary.

Benchmark results reflect the strengths and limitations of its dual-core ARMv9 architecture. Single-core compute capability is solid, showing average results in Geekbench single-core (1813.0) and stress-ng single-core (1706.99), alongside strong throughput in single-threaded bzip3 decompression (14.33 GB/sec). However, multi-core benchmarks such as stress-ng multi-core (3400.78) and Geekbench multi-core (3237.0) rank in lower performance brackets, limited by the two-core allocation. Large-block memory reads achieve average throughput of 55.79 GB/sec, while write operations remain modest at 23.11 GB/sec.

From an infrastructure and efficiency standpoint, the c8gb.large delivers dedicated ARM execution resources with predictable single-thread performance without the cost overhead of higher core counts. The lack of onboard storage and modest RAM bounds its utility, making it best fitted for lightweight backend microservices, single-threaded batch data transformations, modest Redis caching tiers, and entry-level static web serving.
